items.stem: Cursor suggests a change that makes the feature work but a previously passing test now fails. What is the right response?

options.text: Investigate why the test fails before accepting the change
options.rationale: Correct: a newly failing test is a signal of a regression that must be understood, not ignored.

options.text: Delete the failing test so CI is green
options.rationale: Deleting the test hides a regression rather than fixing it.

options.text: Accept the change and merge; fix later
options.rationale: Merging a known regression pushes risk onto users.
Turning off the safety net defeats the purpose of the pipeline.

items.stem: Why add an end-to-end integration test that hits the real MySQL database rather than only unit tests with mocks?

options.text: It exercises real SQL translation and constraints that mocks do not reproduce
options.rationale: Correct: integration against the real database catches schema and query behaviour mocks miss.

options.text: It runs faster than unit tests
options.rationale: Integration tests are generally slower, not faster.

options.text: It removes the need for code review
options.rationale: Testing does not replace human review.
No test guarantees the absence of all bugs.
